public_rationale: Tom's Guide's review, updated May 1, 2024, reported no timers, reminders, ordinary photo-taking or email features [e1]. Engadget reported missing calendar support on April 25 [e2]. Together, these reports support all five omissions in the launch-period product [e1, e2]. TechRadar's May 6 review described saved images from Vision interactions, which establishes image capture for visual analysis but does not establish an ordinary photography feature [e3].
limitations: The cited reviews do not provide a complete feature inventory for the exact May 13 software build [e1, e2, e3].
The finding does not support a broader claim that the R1 could not capture or retain images: Vision interaction images were saved in Rabbit Hole [e3].

our_interpretation: The target is the newly delivered R1's publicly available launch software through the May 13 post. I use April 23–May 13, 2024, as the launch-to-post observation period.
The ordinary reading is usable timer, reminder, calendar, photographic capture, and email-account features.
Photos means an ordinary photo-taking feature. Zitron separately acknowledges the camera's visual-analysis function, so the claim does not deny that the hardware can capture images for analysis.
The judgment concerns the feature list, not the rhetorical criticism of the developers.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous documentation or testing establishes that all five ordinary features were unavailable in the launch-period product.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous documentation or testing establishes usable availability of a named feature. If some were available and others absent, the list is mixed.
